topic: Microsoft Certified: Azure Developer Associate (AZ-204) exam preparation - developing Azure compute solutions, developing for Azure storage, implementing Azure security, monitoring/troubleshooting/optimizing Azure solutions, and connecting to and consuming Azure and third-party services
exam_format: Typically 40-60 questions in 100 minutes, delivered at Pearson VUE test centers or online-proctored. Question formats include multiple choice, multiple response, drag-and-drop, build-list, hot-area, code/complete-the-snippet items, and case studies. Scaled score 100-1000 with a passing score of 700 (700 is a scaled threshold, not 70 percent correct). The certification is valid for one year and renewed free each year via a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn. Exam fee is approximately USD 165 and varies by country and local tax - present it as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current Microsoft pricing. Microsoft periodically updates the skills-measured outline, so tell candidates to verify the current domains and weights on the official Microsoft Learn AZ-204 page before scheduling.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response marked 'Select TWO/THREE', plus code-completion, drag-and-drop, and case-study items; every item is a real-world Azure development scenario asking which service, SDK/API, setting, or code approach is correct - NOT term definitions
audience: Software developers who design, build, test, deploy, and maintain cloud applications and services on Microsoft Azure. Microsoft recommends 1-2 years of professional development experience plus experience with Azure, and proficiency in at least one language supported by the Azure SDKs (C#, Python, JavaScript/Node.js, Java). Comfort with the Azure portal, Azure CLI, REST APIs, JSON, and Git is expected. A strong developer companion to the AZ-104 (Administrator Associate) and AZ-305 (Solutions Architect Expert) courses already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Develop Azure compute solutions
domains.notes: The heaviest domain. Implementing containerized solutions (Azure Container Registry, Azure Container Instances, Azure Container Apps); implementing Azure App Service web apps (deployment, configuration and app settings, autoscale, deployment slots, and slot swapping); and implementing Azure Functions (triggers and bindings, input/output bindings, durable functions and orchestration patterns, hosting/consumption plans). Choosing the correct compute service (App Service vs Functions vs Container Apps), trigger/binding, or scaling approach for a described application requirement.

domains.name: Develop for Azure storage
domains.notes: Developing solutions that use Azure Cosmos DB (choosing APIs, partition keys, consistency levels, request units, change feed, and server-side programming) and Azure Blob Storage (the Storage SDK, uploading/downloading, properties and metadata, lifecycle and access tiers, and leasing). Choosing the correct data store, partition-key design, consistency level, or Blob access pattern for a described scenario, and distinguishing Cosmos DB consistency levels and RU cost implications.

domains.name: Implement Azure security
domains.notes: Implementing user authentication and authorization with the Microsoft Identity platform, Microsoft Entra ID, OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect, the Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL), shared access signatures, and managed identities (system- and user-assigned); and implementing secure cloud solutions with Azure Key Vault (secrets, keys, certificates), app configuration, and managed identity access to resources. Choosing the correct authentication flow, token/credential type, or secret-management approach for a described requirement, and preferring managed identities over stored secrets.

domains.name: Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize Azure solutions
domains.notes: Implementing caching and content delivery (Azure Cache for Redis patterns - cache-aside, expiration/eviction; Azure Front Door / CDN caching and rules) and instrumenting solutions to support monitoring and logging with Azure Monitor, Application Insights (telemetry, custom events/metrics, dependency tracking, availability tests), and Log Analytics/KQL. Choosing the correct caching strategy, telemetry approach, or troubleshooting technique for a described performance or reliability problem.

domains.name: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
domains.notes: Implementing API solutions with Azure API Management (gateways, products, policies, subscriptions); developing event-based solutions with Azure Event Grid and Azure Event Hubs; and developing message-based solutions with Azure Service Bus (queues, topics/subscriptions, sessions, dead-lettering) and Azure Queue Storage. Choosing the correct integration service for a described scenario, and distinguishing events vs messages, Event Grid vs Event Hubs, and Service Bus vs Queue Storage.

extra_guidance: Microsoft Certified: Azure Developer Associate (AZ-204) is Microsoft's core Azure development credential and pairs with the AZ-104 administrator and AZ-305 architect courses in this catalog. The exam is scenario-based and code-aware - the real skill it tests is 'given this application requirement, which Azure service, SDK/API, binding, or code approach is correct,' NOT memorizing definitions. This is a READ-AND-UNDERSTAND developer course - show and explain real code snippets (C# and/or Python using the Azure SDKs), Azure CLI commands, function trigger/binding JSON, and API Management policy XML exactly as they appear, rather than requiring a live paid Azure subscription; make that explicit (a free Azure account or Microsoft Learn sandbox suffices to follow along). Use EXACT current Microsoft product names and call out recent renames: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory), the Microsoft identity platform, MSAL, managed identities, Azure App Service, Azure Functions (durable functions, triggers/bindings), Azure Container Apps, Azure Container Instances, Azure Container Registry, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Blob Storage, Azure Key Vault, Azure Cache for Redis, Azure Front Door, Application Insights, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Kusto Query Language (KQL), Azure API Management, Azure Event Grid, Azure Event Hubs, Azure Service Bus, and Azure Queue Storage - with a one-line note that Azure evolves fast, so verify against current Microsoft Learn docs. The five domain names and weight RANGES above are Microsoft's official AZ-204 skills-measured groupings - present the ranges as Microsoft does and note Microsoft updates weights periodically. Cover the classic AZ-204 traps: App Service vs Functions vs Container Apps, consumption vs premium function plans, durable-functions orchestration patterns, Cosmos DB consistency levels and partition-key design and RU cost, managed identity vs service principal vs SAS vs Key Vault, deployment slots and slot swap, Event Grid vs Event Hubs vs Service Bus (events vs streaming vs messages), Service Bus queues vs topics and dead-lettering, and cache-aside vs other caching patterns. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including the learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 165, varies by country) and note the certification is valid one year with free annual renewal on Microsoft Learn. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 100-minute, ~40-60-question time-management strategy that accounts for case studies and code items. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (AWS/Google/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
